verses.translation: A supplicant asked for a punishment bound to happen[1748]
verses.footnotes: [1748]- In the Hereafter. Disbelievers had challenged the Prophet (ﷺ) by invoking Allāh to bring on His punishment. See 8:32.

verses.translation: To the disbelievers; of it there is no preventer.
[It is] from Allāh, owner of the ways of ascent.

verses.arabic: تَعْرُجُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ إِلَيْهِ فِى يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُۥ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ
verses.translation: The angels and the Spirit [i.e., Gabriel] will ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years.

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, feminine, singular

verses.translation: So be patient with gracious patience.
Indeed, they see it [as] distant,

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, plural

verses.translation: But We see it [as] near.
On the Day the sky will be like murky oil,[1749]

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, feminine, singular

verses.translation: And the mountains will be like wool,[1750]
verses.footnotes: [1750]- i.e., in the process of disintegration.

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, feminine, singular

verses.translation: And no friend will ask [anything of] a friend,

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, singular

verses.arabic: يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ يَوَدُّ ٱلْمُجْرِمُ لَوْ يَفْتَدِى مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِئِذٍۭ بِبَنِيهِ
verses.translation: They will be shown each other. The criminal will wish that he could be ransomed from the punishment of that Day by his children

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, plural, passive

words.gloss: They will be made to see each other

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, singular
Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, singular

verses.translation: And his wife and his brother
And his nearest kindred who shelter him

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, feminine, singular

verses.arabic: وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ
verses.translation: And whoever is on earth entirely [so] then it could save him.

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, singular

verses.translation: No![1751] Indeed, it is the Flame [of Hell],
verses.footnotes: [1751]- An emphatic refusal meaning "It is not to be."

verses.translation: A remover of exteriors.[1752]
verses.footnotes: [1752]- This refers to the skin of the head or of the body or to the body extremities - which will be burned away.

words.gloss: of the skin of the head

verses.translation: It invites he who turned his back [on truth] and went away [from obedience]

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, feminine, singular

verses.translation: And collected [wealth] and hoarded.
Indeed, mankind was created anxious:

segments.description: Verb — perfect, 3rd person, masculine, singular, passive

verses.translation: When evil touches him, impatient,
And when good touches him, withholding [of it],
Except the observers of prayer -
Those who are constant in their prayer
And those within whose wealth is a known right[1753]
verses.footnotes: [1753]- i.e., a specified share, meaning the obligatory zakāh.

verses.translation: For the petitioner and the deprived -
And those who believe in the Day of Recompense

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, plural

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم مِّنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّهِم مُّشْفِقُونَ
verses.translation: And those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord -
Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not that from which one is safe -
And those who guard their private parts

verses.arabic: إِلَّا عَلَىٰٓ أَزْوَٰجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ
verses.translation: Except from their wives or those their right hands possess,[1754] for indeed, they are not to be blamed -

verses.arabic: فَمَنِ ٱبْتَغَىٰ وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْعَادُونَ
verses.translation: But whoever seeks beyond that, then they are the transgressors -
And those who are to their trusts and promises attentive
And those who are in their testimonies upright
And those who [carefully] maintain their prayer:

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, plural

verses.translation: They will be in gardens,[1755] honored.
So what is [the matter] with those who disbelieve, hastening [from] before you, [O Muḥammad],
[To sit] on [your] right and [your] left in separate groups?[1756]
verses.footnotes: [1756]- They sat at a distance in order to oppose and mock the Prophet (ﷺ), claiming that they would enter Paradise before the believers.

verses.arabic: أَيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِئٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُدْخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍ
verses.translation: Does every person among them aspire to enter a garden of pleasure?

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, singular
Verb — imperfect, subjunctive, 3rd person, masculine, singular, passive

verses.translation: No! Indeed, We have created them from that which they know.[1757]
verses.footnotes: [1757]- i.e., a liquid disdained. So how can they expect to enter Paradise except by the will of their Creator?

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, plural

verses.arabic: فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْمَشَٰرِقِ وَٱلْمَغَٰرِبِ إِنَّا لَقَٰدِرُونَ
verses.translation: So I swear by the Lord of [all] risings and settings[1758] that indeed We are able
verses.footnotes: [1758]- i.e., Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā), who determines the point at which the sun, moon and stars rise and set according to season and every position of observation.

verses.arabic: عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّبَدِّلَ خَيْرًا مِّنْهُمْ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ
verses.translation: To replace them with better than them; and We are not to be outdone.

verses.arabic: فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُوا۟ وَيَلْعَبُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ يُلَٰقُوا۟ يَوْمَهُمُ ٱلَّذِى يُوعَدُونَ
verses.translation: So leave them to converse vainly and amuse themselves until they meet their Day which they are promised -

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, jussive, 3rd person, masculine, plural
Verb — imperfect, jussive, 3rd person, masculine, plural
Verb — imperfect, subjunctive, 3rd person, masculine, plural
Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, plural, passive

verses.arabic: يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلْأَجْدَاثِ سِرَاعًا كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَىٰ نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ
verses.translation: The Day they will emerge from the graves rapidly as if they were, toward an erected idol, hastening.[1759]
verses.footnotes: [1759]- i.e., just as they used to race, whenever an idol was newly appointed, to be the first of its worshippers.

segments.description: Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, plural
Verb — imperfect, indicative, 3rd person, masculine, plural

verses.arabic: خَٰشِعَةً أَبْصَٰرُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمُ ٱلَّذِى كَانُوا۟ يُوعَدُونَ
verses.translation: Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them. That is the Day which they had been promised.
